-- Author: @toskua
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.Submodule
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Finiteness.Cardinality
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.FractionRing
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.Integer

/-!
# Clearing a finite module into the lattice of a field basis

A single nonzero denominator carries the image of a finite module into
the full span over the original domain of a finite fraction-field basis.
The denominator is derived from the actual generator coordinates.
-/

@[expose] public section
noncomputable section

universe u v w z t

namespace Module.Basis

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
variable {K : Type v} [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
variable {V : Type w} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [Module R V] [IsScalarTower R K V]
variable {M : Type z} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]

/-- The actual coordinates of a finite generating family earn a common
nonzero scalar carrying its entire image into the original domain span of
a finite fraction-field basis. Neither freeness of the source module nor
normality of the domain is needed. -/
theorem exists_scalar_image_mem_span {ι : Type t} [Finite ι]
    (b : Basis ι K V) (f : M →ₗ[R] V) :
    ∃ a : R, a ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x : M, a • f x ∈ Submodule.span R (Set.range b) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨n, s, hs⟩ := Module.Finite.exists_fin (R := R) (M := M)
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite
    (nonZeroDivisors R) (fun p : Fin n × ι => b.repr (f (s p.1)) p.2)
  refine ⟨a, mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mp a.property, ?_⟩
  let q : Submodule R M := (Submodule.span R (Set.range b)).comap (a.val • f)
  have hgen : ∀ i : Fin n, s i ∈ q := by
    intro i
    change a.val • f (s i) ∈ Submodule.span R (Set.range b)
    apply (b.mem_span_iff_repr_mem R _).mpr
    intro j
    have h := ha (i, j)
    change b.repr.toLinearMap (a.val • f (s i)) j ∈ Set.range (algebraMap R K)
    rw [b.repr.toLinearMap.map_smul_of_tower]
    exact h
  have hq : ⊤ ≤ q := by
    rw [← hs]
    apply Submodule.span_le.mpr
    rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
    exact hgen i
  intro x
  exact hq (show x ∈ (⊤ : Submodule R M) from trivial)

end Module.Basis

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.Finset.Basic
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant

/-!
# Determinants after basis-column normalization

This file records the determinant factorization obtained by extracting a
possibly different power of one scalar from every column of a linear
endomorphism.

## Main result

* `LinearMap.det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis`: if, on a finite basis
  `b`, two endomorphisms satisfy

  ```text
  f (b i) = π ^ c i • g (b i),
  ```

  then

  ```text
  det f = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * det g.
  ```
* `LinearMap.UniformizerColumnNormalization`: bundles the basis, extracted
  exponents, normalized endomorphism, and column identities; its `det_eq`
  theorem applies the factorization directly.

The statement is valid over an arbitrary commutative ring.  In particular,
`π` need not be regular or a uniformizer; those hypotheses belong only to
applications which construct `g` by dividing the columns of `f`.  The
explicit finite basis supplies the determinant data, so no separate
`Module.Free` or `Module.Finite` instance is required.

## Informal proof

Write both endomorphisms in the basis `b`.  The hypothesis says that column
`i` of the matrix of `f` is column `i` of the matrix of `g`, multiplied by
`π ^ c i`.  Hence

```text
matrix(f) = matrix(g) * diagonal(i ↦ π ^ c i).
```

Taking determinants turns the matrix product into a product.  The determinant
of the diagonal factor is `∏ i, π ^ c i`, and collecting powers of the common
base `π` changes this product to `π ^ ∑ i, c i`.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uM uI

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM} {ι : Type uI}
variable [CommRing R] [Fintype ι]
variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]

/-- Extracting the power `π ^ c i` from basis column `i` extracts the sum of
the exponents from the determinant.

This is a columnwise factorization theorem, not a division theorem: the
normalized endomorphism `g` and the displayed basis equalities are supplied
as data.  Consequently no regularity assumption on `π` is required. -/
theorem det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis
    (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (π : R) (c : ι → ℕ)
    (f g : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, f (b i) = π ^ c i • g (b i)) :
    f.det = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * g.det := by
  classical
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix b b f =
        LinearMap.toMatrix b b g * Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i) := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, h j, map_smul, Matrix.mul_diagonal,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Finsupp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]
  calc
    f.det = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b f).det :=
      (LinearMap.det_toMatrix b f).symm
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b g *
          Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i)).det := by rw [hmatrix]
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b g).det *
          (Matrix.diagonal (fun i ↦ π ^ c i)).det := by
      rw [Matrix.det_mul]
    _ = g.det * ∏ i, π ^ c i := by
      rw [LinearMap.det_toMatrix, Matrix.det_diagonal]
    _ = π ^ (∑ i, c i) * g.det := by
      rw [Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum]
      exact mul_comm _ _

/-- Basis-indexed data exhibiting an endomorphism as columnwise powers of
one scalar times a normalized endomorphism. -/
structure UniformizerColumnNormalization {R : Type uR} {M : Type uM}
    [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (pi : R) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) where
  index : Type uI
  indexFintype : Fintype index
  basis : Module.Basis index R M
  exponent : index → ℕ
  normalized : M →ₗ[R] M
  apply_basis : ∀ i,
    f (basis i) = pi ^ exponent i • normalized (basis i)

namespace UniformizerColumnNormalization

variable {pi : R} {f : M →ₗ[R] M}

/-- Construct bundled column-normalization data from basiswise divisibility
witnesses.  The normalized endomorphism is the linear map sending each basis
vector to a chosen quotient column. -/
noncomputable def ofExists (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (pi : R)
    (c : ι → ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ y : M, f (b i) = pi ^ c i • y) :
    UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f where
  index := ι
  indexFintype := inferInstance
  basis := b
  exponent := c
  normalized := b.constr R fun i ↦ Classical.choose (h i)
  apply_basis := fun i ↦ by
    rw [Module.Basis.constr_basis]
    exact Classical.choose_spec (h i)

/-- Total scalar exponent extracted from all basis columns. -/
noncomputable def totalExponent
    (D : UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f) : ℕ := by
  letI : Fintype D.index := D.indexFintype
  exact ∑ i, D.exponent i

@[simp]
theorem totalExponent_ofExists (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (pi : R)
    (c : ι → ℕ) (f : M →ₗ[R] M)
    (h : ∀ i, ∃ y : M, f (b i) = pi ^ c i • y) :
    (ofExists b pi c f h).totalExponent = ∑ i, c i :=
  rfl

/-- Determinant factorization supplied by bundled column-normalization
data. -/
theorem det_eq (D : UniformizerColumnNormalization pi f) :
    f.det = pi ^ D.totalExponent * D.normalized.det := by
  let _ : Fintype D.index := D.indexFintype
  exact det_eq_pow_sum_mul_det_of_apply_basis
    D.basis pi D.exponent f D.normalized D.apply_basis

end UniformizerColumnNormalization

end LinearMap

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Block

/-!
# Determinants of dependent componentwise endomorphisms

Mathlib's `LinearMap.det_pi` computes the determinant of a componentwise
endomorphism of `ι → M`, where every component is the same finite free
module.  This file proves the dependent-family version: the modules `M i`
may have different ranks.

## Informal proof

Choose a finite basis `b i` of each component `M i`.  The dependent Pi basis
`Pi.basis b` is indexed by the sigma type of all component basis indices.
In that basis the componentwise endomorphism has matrix

```text
Matrix.blockDiagonal' (fun i => matrix (f i)).
```

Indeed, a basis vector supported in component `j` stays in component `j`, so
every off-diagonal block is zero, while the `j`-th diagonal block is exactly
the matrix of `f j`.

For completeness, the required determinant formula for unequal block sizes
is proved first.  Give the finite outer index an arbitrary linear order and
view `blockDiagonal'` as block triangular.  The block-triangular determinant
theorem expresses its determinant as the product of its square diagonal
blocks.  The fiber of `Sigma.fst` over `i` is canonically equivalent to the
index type of the `i`-th block, so determinant invariance under reindexing
identifies that square block with the original matrix.  Applying this matrix
formula to the dependent Pi basis gives the result.

## Reconstructing a block-diagonal endomorphism

For an arbitrary endomorphism `F` of a finite dependent product, its `(i,j)`
block is the composite

```text
M j --single j--> (∀ i, M i) --F--> (∀ i, M i) --proj i--> M i.
```

Suppose every block with `i ≠ j` is zero.  Decompose an arbitrary vector as
the finite sum `∑ j, Pi.single j (x j)` and apply linearity of `F`.  After
evaluating at coordinate `i`, all terms except `j = i` vanish by the block
hypothesis.  The surviving term is the diagonal block applied to `x i`.
Function and linear-map extensionality therefore identify `F` with the
componentwise endomorphism assembled from its diagonal blocks.  This argument
uses neither matrices nor finite-free hypotheses.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators

universe uR uI uM uK

namespace Matrix

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {κ : ι → Type uK} [∀ i, Fintype (κ i)]

/-- The index type of one block is equivalent to the corresponding fiber of
the sigma-type block projection. -/
private noncomputable def sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (i : ι) :
    κ i ≃ {x : Sigma κ // x.1 = i} :=
  Equiv.ofBijective
    (fun j => ⟨⟨i, j⟩, rfl⟩)
    ⟨fun _ _ h => sigma_mk_injective (congrArg Subtype.val h), fun x => by
      rcases x with ⟨⟨j, x⟩, hj⟩
      change j = i at hj
      subst j
      exact ⟨x, rfl⟩⟩

omit [Fintype ι] [∀ i, Fintype (κ i)] in
private theorem toSquareBlock_blockDiagonal'_eq_reindex
    [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) (i : ι) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).toSquareBlock Sigma.fst i =
      Matrix.reindex (sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i)
        (sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i) (A i) := by
  ext ⟨⟨j, x⟩, hj⟩ ⟨⟨k, y⟩, hk⟩
  change j = i at hj
  change k = i at hk
  subst j
  subst k
  simp only [Matrix.toSquareBlock_def, Matrix.of_apply,
    Matrix.reindex_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply,
    Matrix.blockDiagonal'_apply_eq]
  let e := sigmaBlockFiberEquiv (κ := κ) i
  change A i x y =
    A i (e.symm ⟨⟨i, x⟩, rfl⟩) (e.symm ⟨⟨i, y⟩, rfl⟩)
  have hx : e.symm ⟨⟨i, x⟩, rfl⟩ = x := by
    apply e.symm_apply_eq.mpr
    apply Subtype.ext
    rfl
  have hy : e.symm ⟨⟨i, y⟩, rfl⟩ = y := by
    apply e.symm_apply_eq.mpr
    apply Subtype.ext
    rfl
  rw [hx, hy]

private theorem det_blockDiagonal'_of_linearOrder
    [DecidableEq ι] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)] [LinearOrder ι]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).det = ∏ i, (A i).det := by
  rw [(Matrix.blockTriangular_blockDiagonal' A).det_fintype]
  apply Finset.prod_congr rfl
  intro i _
  rw [toSquareBlock_blockDiagonal'_eq_reindex,
    Matrix.det_reindex_self]

/-- The determinant of a finite dependent block-diagonal matrix is the
product of the determinants of its blocks. -/
theorem det_blockDiagonal' [DecidableEq ι] [∀ i, DecidableEq (κ i)]
    (A : ∀ i, Matrix (κ i) (κ i) R) :
    (Matrix.blockDiagonal' A).det = ∏ i, (A i).det := by
  classical
  let horder : LinearOrder ι := linearOrderOfSTO WellOrderingRel
  exact @det_blockDiagonal'_of_linearOrder R _ ι _ κ _ _ _ horder A

end Matrix

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI}
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]

/-- The `(i,j)` block of an endomorphism of a dependent product: include the
`j`-th component, apply the endomorphism, then project to component `i`. -/
noncomputable def dependentPiBlock
    (F : (∀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] ∀ i, M i) (i j : ι) : M j →ₗ[R] M i := by
  classical
  exact (LinearMap.proj i).comp (F.comp (LinearMap.single R M j))

/-- A finite dependent-product endomorphism with zero off-diagonal blocks is
the componentwise endomorphism assembled from its diagonal blocks. -/
theorem eq_pi_diagonal_of_dependentPiBlock_eq_zero
    [Finite ι]
    (F : (∀ i, M i) →ₗ[R] ∀ i, M i)
    (hF : ∀ i j : ι, i ≠ j → dependentPiBlock F i j = 0) :
    F = LinearMap.pi fun i => (dependentPiBlock F i i).comp (LinearMap.proj i) := by
  classical
  let _ : Fintype ι := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  apply LinearMap.ext
  intro x
  funext i
  change F x i = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i)
  calc
    F x i = F (∑ j, Pi.single j (x j)) i := by
      rw [LinearMap.sum_single_apply]
    _ = ∑ j, F (Pi.single j (x j)) i := by
      rw [map_sum, Finset.sum_apply]
    _ = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i) := by
      change (∑ j, dependentPiBlock F i j (x j)) = dependentPiBlock F i i (x i)
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i]
      · intro j _ hji
        rw [hF i j hji.symm, LinearMap.zero_apply]
      · simp

variable [Fintype ι]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- Determinant of a componentwise endomorphism of a finite dependent
product.  Unlike `LinearMap.det_pi`, the component modules may have unequal
ranks. -/
theorem det_pi_dependent (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).det =
      ∏ i, (f i).det := by
  classical
  let b := fun i => Module.Free.chooseBasis R (M i)
  let B := Pi.basis b
  simp_rw [← LinearMap.det_toMatrix B, ← LinearMap.det_toMatrix (b _)]
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix B B
          (LinearMap.pi fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i)) =
        Matrix.blockDiagonal'
          (fun i => LinearMap.toMatrix (b i) (b i) (f i)) := by
    ext ⟨i, x⟩ ⟨j, y⟩
    simp only [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply', B, Pi.basis_apply, Pi.basis_repr,
      LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
      LinearMap.coe_proj, Function.eval,
      Matrix.blockDiagonal'_apply]
    split_ifs with h
    · subst j
      simp
    · simp [h]
  rw [hmatrix, Matrix.det_blockDiagonal']

end LinearMap

namespace LinearEquiv

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- The determinant of a dependent product of linear equivalences is the
product of their determinants. -/
theorem det_piCongrRight (f : ∀ i, M i ≃ₗ[R] M i) :
    LinearEquiv.det (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight f) =
      ∏ i, LinearEquiv.det (f i) := by
  apply Units.ext
  rw [LinearEquiv.coe_det, Units.coe_prod]
  have hmap : (LinearEquiv.piCongrRight f).toLinearMap =
      LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).toLinearMap.comp
        (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro x
    funext i
    rfl
  rw [hmap, LinearMap.det_pi_dependent]
  simp only [LinearEquiv.coe_det]

end LinearEquiv

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Determinant
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Basis.Defs

/-!
# Determinants after transporting scalar coefficients

Let `e : R ≃+* S`, and let the same additive group `M` carry compatible
`R`- and `S`-module structures.  Compatibility means

```text
e c • x = c • x.
```

Suppose `fR : M →ₗ[R] M` and `fS : M →ₗ[S] M` have the same underlying
function.  Given a finite `R`-basis of `M`, this file proves

```text
e fR.det = fS.det.
```

## Informal proof

Let `b : Basis ι R M`, and use `b.mapCoeffs e h` as the corresponding
`S`-basis.  The transported basis has the same vectors as `b`.  Moreover,
`Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_repr` identifies the entire representation
equivalence. In particular, the `i`-th coordinate of any
vector in the transported basis is obtained by applying `e` to its `i`-th
coordinate in `b`.

Consequently, for every pair of basis indices `i,j`,

```text
toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS i j
  = e (toMatrix b b fR i j).
```

Indeed, both entries are the corresponding coordinate of the common value
`fS (b j) = fR (b j)`.  Matrix extensionality therefore identifies the
`S`-matrix with `Matrix.map e` of the `R`-matrix.

Now rewrite both linear-map determinants using `LinearMap.det_toMatrix`.
The matrix equality and `RingEquiv.map_det` give

```text
e (det (toMatrix b b fR))
  = det (toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS),
```

which is the desired equality.

The argument uses only commutative rings.  Empty finite bases are included:
both matrix determinants are the empty determinant `1`, and the same proof
applies unchanged.

## API novelty

The closest standard result is `Algebra.norm_eq_of_ringEquiv`, but that
compares determinants only for multiplication endomorphisms in algebra
norms.  It does not apply to arbitrary linear endomorphisms.  The ingredients
used here—`Basis.mapCoeffs_repr`, `RingEquiv.map_det`, and
`LinearMap.det_toMatrix`—do not already package this general transport law.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open Module

universe uR uS uM uι

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
variable {M : Type uM} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M]
variable {ι : Type uι} [Finite ι]

/-- Determinants commute with transport along a scalar-ring equivalence when
the scalar actions and the underlying endomorphism agree. -/
theorem det_mapCoeffs (e : R ≃+* S)
    (h : ∀ (c : R) (x : M), e c • x = c • x)
    (b : Basis ι R M) (fR : M →ₗ[R] M) (fS : M →ₗ[S] M)
    (hf : ∀ x, fS x = fR x) :
    e fR.det = fS.det := by
  let _ : Fintype ι := Fintype.ofFinite ι
  classical
  have hmatrix :
      LinearMap.toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h) (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS =
        (LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).map e := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      Basis.mapCoeffs_apply, Basis.mapCoeffs_repr,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
    change e (b.repr (fS (b j)) i) = e (b.repr (fR (b j)) i)
    rw [hf]
  calc
    e fR.det = e (LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).det := by
      rw [LinearMap.det_toMatrix]
    _ = ((LinearMap.toMatrix b b fR).map e).det := e.map_det _
    _ = (LinearMap.toMatrix (b.mapCoeffs e h)
        (b.mapCoeffs e h) fS).det := by rw [hmatrix]
    _ = fS.det := LinearMap.det_toMatrix _ _

end LinearMap

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.BaseChange
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.ResidueField.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Quotient

/-!
# Linear endomorphisms after quotient base change

Let `S` be a finite free algebra over a commutative ring `R`, let `I` be an
ideal of `R`, and let `f : S →ₗ[R] S`.  This file transports the ordinary
scalar extension of `f` across the canonical algebra equivalence

```text
S / I S  ≃  (R / I) ⊗[R] S.
```

The resulting endomorphism `f.quotientBaseChange I` sends the class
of `x` to the class of `f x`, and its determinant is the reduction of
`det f` modulo `I`.

For a local base ring, bijectivity of the residue endomorphism therefore
shows that `det f` is a unit.  The bundled determinant unit has residue equal
to the determinant unit of the induced residue equivalence.

## Main declarations

* `LinearMap.quotientBaseChange`: quotient-valued scalar extension of an
  arbitrary finite-free algebra endomorphism.
* `LinearMap.quotientBaseChange_mk`: representative formula.
* `LinearMap.det_quotientBaseChange`: determinant commutes with reduction.
* `LinearMap.isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange`: local unit
  detection from a bijective residue map.
* `LinearMap.detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange`: the resulting determinant
  unit, with its value and residue formulas.

## Informal proof

The canonical equivalence
`Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I` sends the class of
`x : S` to `1 ⊗ x`.  Conjugate the scalar extension
`f.baseChange (R / I)` by the inverse of this equivalence.  Since scalar
extension sends `1 ⊗ x` to `1 ⊗ f x`, conjugation gives the representative
formula.

Determinants are invariant under conjugation, and
`LinearMap.det_baseChange` identifies the determinant of the scalar extension
with `Ideal.Quotient.mk I (det f)`.  This proves determinant reduction without
choosing a basis of either quotient presentation.

Now suppose `R` is local and use its maximal ideal.  If the quotient map is
bijective, it is a linear equivalence, so its determinant is a unit and in
particular is nonzero in the residue field.  Determinant reduction says that
this nonzero element is the residue of `det f`.  An element of a local ring
has nonzero residue exactly when it is a unit.  Bundling that unit and applying
the same determinant equality proves the final residue formula.
-/

@[expose] public section

noncomputable section

set_option autoImplicit false

universe uR uS

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} {S : Type uS}
variable [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]

/-- Scalar extension of an algebra endomorphism to `R / I`, transported from
the tensor-product presentation to the quotient presentation `S / I S`.

This is the arbitrary-linear-map analogue of quotient base change for
algebra norms; it reuses the same canonical tensor/quotient equivalence. -/
noncomputable def quotientBaseChange (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) :
    (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S)) →ₗ[R ⧸ I]
      (S ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R S)) := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  exact e.symm.toLinearEquiv.conj (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I))

/-- Quotient base change sends a represented class to the class of its image
under the original endomorphism. -/
@[simp]
theorem quotientBaseChange_mk (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) (x : S) :
    f.quotientBaseChange I
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R S)) x) =
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (f x) := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  apply e.injective
  simp [quotientBaseChange, e]

section Finite

variable [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S]

/-- The determinant of quotient base change is the reduction of the original
determinant modulo the base ideal. -/
theorem det_quotientBaseChange (f : S →ₗ[R] S) (I : Ideal R) :
    (f.quotientBaseChange I).det = Ideal.Quotient.mk I f.det := by
  let e := Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor S I
  change LinearMap.det
      (e.symm.toLinearEquiv.conj (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I))) = _
  calc
    _ = LinearMap.det (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I)) := by
      rw [LinearEquiv.conj_apply, LinearMap.comp_assoc]
      exact LinearMap.det_conj
        (f.baseChange (R ⧸ I)) e.symm.toLinearEquiv
    _ = _ := LinearMap.det_baseChange f

section Local

variable [IsLocalRing R]

/-- If the endomorphism induced on the closed fiber of a finite free algebra
is bijective, then the original determinant is a unit of the local base. -/
theorem isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    IsUnit f.det := by
  apply (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit f.det).mp
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) f.det ≠ 0
  rw [← det_quotientBaseChange]
  exact (LinearEquiv.ofBijective _ hf).isUnit_det'.ne_zero

/-- The determinant unit supplied by bijectivity of the closed-fiber
endomorphism. -/
noncomputable def detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) : Rˣ :=
  (isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange f hf).unit

/-- The underlying value of the determinant unit is the original
determinant. -/
@[simp]
theorem coe_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    (detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange f hf : R) = f.det :=
  (isUnit_det_of_bijective_quotientBaseChange f hf).unit_spec

/-- The residue of the bundled determinant unit is the determinant unit of
the induced closed-fiber equivalence. -/
theorem residue_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange
    (f : S →ₗ[R] S)
    (hf : Function.Bijective
      (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))) :
    Units.map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)).toMonoidHom
        (detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange f hf) =
      LinearEquiv.det
        (LinearEquiv.ofBijective
          (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) hf) := by
  apply Units.ext
  simp only [Units.coe_map, LinearEquiv.coe_det,
    coe_detUnitOfBijectiveQuotientBaseChange]
  change Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) f.det =
    (f.quotientBaseChange (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)).det
  rw [det_quotientBaseChange]

end Local

end Finite

end LinearMap

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Pi
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.FiniteFiltration

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials of dependent componentwise endomorphisms

Mathlib's `LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap` computes the characteristic
polynomial of a binary product endomorphism.  This file proves the
dependent-family version over a finite index type: the modules `M i` may
have different ranks, and the characteristic polynomial of the
componentwise endomorphism of `∀ i, M i` is the product of the component
characteristic polynomials.  It is the characteristic-polynomial analogue
of `LinearMap.det_pi_dependent` in
`MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Determinant.DependentPi`.

## Main results

* `LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent`: the characteristic polynomial of a
  componentwise endomorphism of a finite dependent product is the product
  of the component characteristic polynomials.
* `Algebra.lmul_charpoly_eq_of_algEquiv`: the characteristic polynomial of
  left multiplication is invariant under algebra equivalence, paralleling
  `Algebra.norm_eq_of_algEquiv`.
* `Algebra.lmul_charpoly_pi_apply`: the characteristic polynomial of left
  multiplication by an element of a finite dependent product of algebras
  is the product of the component characteristic polynomials.

## Informal proof

The proof follows the pattern of `Algebra.norm_pi_apply` in
`MathlibExt.RingTheory.Norm.FiniteProduct`, rather than the block-diagonal
matrix computation used for determinants: `Matrix.charpoly`, unlike
`Matrix.det`, takes `DecidableEq` and `Fintype` instance arguments, and
the block-triangular route produces diagonal-block characteristic
polynomials whose fiber instances mix two different `DecidableEq`
sources, which do not unify with synthesized instances.  The induction
route only ever uses the ambient module instances.

For a product indexed by `Fin n`, induct on `n`.  The empty product is a
zero module, so its characteristic polynomial is `1`.  At the successor
step, split a dependent function into its zeroth coordinate and its tail.
Conjugating the componentwise endomorphism by this linear equivalence
gives the binary product of the head endomorphism and the componentwise
tail endomorphism; `LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap`, conjugation invariance,
and the induction hypothesis give the result.  Finally, reindex an
arbitrary finite type by `Fin (Fintype.card ι)`; conjugation invariance
of the characteristic polynomial and invariance of a finite product under
reindexing finish the proof.  Left multiplication on a product algebra
is componentwise by definition, and an algebra equivalence conjugates
left multiplication by `x` to left multiplication by its image, giving
the two algebra corollaries.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false
noncomputable section

open scoped BigOperators
open Polynomial

universe uR uI uM uK

namespace LinearMap

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]

/-- Split a dependent product over `Fin (n + 1)` into its head and tail
factors, as a linear equivalence. -/
private def piFinSuccLinearEquiv {n : ℕ} (M : Fin (n + 1) → Type uM)
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)] :
    (∀ i, M i) ≃ₗ[R] M 0 × (∀ i : Fin n, M (Fin.succ i)) where
  toFun f := (f 0, Fin.tail f)
  invFun p := Fin.cons p.1 p.2
  left_inv f := Fin.cons_self_tail f
  right_inv p := by
    ext
    · exact Fin.cons_zero p.1 p.2
    · exact Fin.cons_succ p.1 p.2 _
  map_add' _ _ := rfl
  map_smul' _ _ := rfl

/-- Conjugating a componentwise endomorphism over `Fin (n + 1)` by the
head-tail equivalence gives the binary product of the head endomorphism
and the componentwise tail endomorphism. -/
private theorem piFinSuccLinearEquiv_conj_pi {n : ℕ}
    {M : Fin (n + 1) → Type uM} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)]
    [∀ i, Module R (M i)] (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (piFinSuccLinearEquiv (R := R) M).conj
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))) =
      (f 0).prodMap
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i : Fin n => (f i.succ).comp
          (LinearMap.proj i))) := by
  apply LinearMap.ext
  rintro ⟨x, y⟩
  apply Prod.ext
  · rfl
  · funext i
    rfl

/-- The characteristic polynomial of a componentwise endomorphism of a
`Fin n`-indexed dependent product is the product of the component
characteristic polynomials. -/
private theorem charpoly_pi_dependent_fin {n : ℕ} {M : Fin n → Type uM}
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
    [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]
    (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    have : Subsingleton (∀ i, M i) :=
      ⟨fun _ _ => funext fun i => i.elim0⟩
    rw [LinearMap.charpoly_eq_one_of_subsingleton]
    simp
  | succ n ih =>
    calc
      (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
          ((piFinSuccLinearEquiv (R := R) M).conj
            (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp
              (LinearMap.proj i)))).charpoly :=
        (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj _ _).symm
      _ = (f 0).charpoly *
            (LinearMap.pi (fun i : Fin n => (f i.succ).comp
              (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly := by
        rw [piFinSuccLinearEquiv_conj_pi, LinearMap.charpoly_prodMap]
      _ = (f 0).charpoly * ∏ i : Fin n, (f i.succ).charpoly := by
        rw [ih (fun i => f i.succ)]
      _ = ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
        rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]

variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι]
variable {M : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, AddCommGroup (M i)] [∀ i, Module R (M i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (M i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (M i)]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of a componentwise endomorphism of a finite
dependent product. The component modules may have unequal ranks. -/
theorem charpoly_pi_dependent (f : ∀ i, M i →ₗ[R] M i) :
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (f i).charpoly := by
  classical
  let e := Fintype.equivFin ι
  have hconj : (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).conj
        (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))) =
      LinearMap.pi (fun j => (f (e.symm j)).comp (LinearMap.proj j)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro g
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := (LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).surjective g
    funext j
    simp [e]
  calc
    (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp (LinearMap.proj i))).charpoly =
        ((LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft' R M e).conj
          (LinearMap.pi (fun i => (f i).comp
            (LinearMap.proj i)))).charpoly :=
      (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj _ _).symm
    _ = ∏ j, (f (e.symm j)).charpoly := by
      rw [hconj, charpoly_pi_dependent_fin]
    _ = ∏ i, (f i).charpoly :=
      Fintype.prod_equiv e.symm _ _ (fun _ => rfl)

end LinearMap

namespace Algebra

variable {R : Type uR} [CommRing R]
variable {S : Type uM} {T : Type uK} [Ring S] [Ring T]
variable [Algebra R S] [Algebra R T]
variable [Module.Free R S] [Module.Finite R S]
variable [Module.Free R T] [Module.Finite R T]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of left multiplication is invariant under
algebra equivalence: an algebra equivalence conjugates left multiplication
by `x` to left multiplication by the image of `x`.  This parallels
`Algebra.norm_eq_of_algEquiv`. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_eq_of_algEquiv (e : S ≃ₐ[R] T) (x : S) :
    (Algebra.lmul R T (e x)).charpoly =
      (Algebra.lmul R S x).charpoly := by
  rw [← LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj e.toLinearEquiv (Algebra.lmul R S x)]
  congr 1
  ext y
  simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]

variable {ι : Type uI} [Fintype ι] {A : ι → Type uM}
variable [∀ i, Ring (A i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (A i)]
variable [∀ i, Module.Free R (A i)] [∀ i, Module.Finite R (A i)]

/-- The characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by an element of a
finite dependent product of algebras is the product of the characteristic
polynomials of left multiplication by its components. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_pi_apply (q : ∀ i, A i) :
    (Algebra.lmul R (∀ i, A i) q).charpoly =
      ∏ i, (Algebra.lmul R (A i) (q i)).charpoly := by
  classical
  have hmul : Algebra.lmul R (∀ i, A i) q =
      LinearMap.pi (fun i => (Algebra.lmul R (A i) (q i)).comp
        (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro y
    funext i
    rfl
  rw [hmul, LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent]

end Algebra

end

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.Basic

/-!
# Minimal and characteristic polynomials of left multiplication

If the natural degree of `minpoly K x` is the finrank of the
finite-dimensional algebra `E`, the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x` is the minimal polynomial. Both are monic, the
minimal polynomial divides the characteristic polynomial by the existing
Cayley--Hamilton evaluation theorem, and their natural degrees agree.

The underlying polynomial-evaluation, integrality and minimal-polynomial
transport facts are supplied by Mathlib's algebra-homomorphism APIs.
The algebra need not be commutative, reduced or a domain. Finite
dimensionality already supplies the integrality of `x`.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace LinearMap

section Primitive

variable {K E : Type*} [Field K] [Ring E] [Algebra K E]
  [FiniteDimensional K E]

/-- If the minimal polynomial of `x` has natural degree equal to the
finrank of the algebra, it is the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x`. Finite dimensionality supplies integrality. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_eq_minpoly_of_natDegree_eq_finrank
    (x : E) (hDeg : (minpoly K x).natDegree = Module.finrank K E) :
    (Algebra.lmul K E x).charpoly = minpoly K x := by
  have hdvd : minpoly K x ∣ (Algebra.lmul K E x).charpoly :=
    minpoly.dvd K x (Algebra.aeval_self_charpoly_lmul x)
  apply Polynomial.eq_of_monic_of_dvd_of_natDegree_le
    (minpoly.monic (IsIntegral.of_finite K x)) (charpoly_monic _) hdvd
  rw [charpoly_natDegree, hDeg]

end Primitive

end LinearMap

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.ToMatrix
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Charpoly.Basic
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.LocalRing.Quotient

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials under quotient and base-ring equivalence

* `Algebra.charpoly_lmul_quotient_maximalIdeal_map`: over a local
  ring `R`, the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by the
  class of `s` on the special fiber `S ⧸ 𝔪S` is the reduction modulo
  `𝔪` of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by `s`
  on `S`.
* `Algebra.charpoly_lmul_map_ringEquiv`: if the scalars of an
  algebra are reindexed along a ring equivalence `φ : k ≃+* k'`, the
  characteristic polynomial of left multiplication is mapped along
  `φ`.

Both proofs compare matrices in corresponding bases: the reduced basis
`IsLocalRing.basisQuotient` in the first case, and the transferred
basis `Module.Basis.mapCoeffs` (the same vectors, with coordinates
reindexed along `φ.symm`) in the second; in each case the matrices
differ entrywise by the relevant ring homomorphism and
`Matrix.charpoly_map` concludes.

The freeness and finiteness instances needed to *form* the
characteristic polynomials in the statements are not automatic (the
quotient module is free only because `basisQuotient` is a basis, and
finiteness over the reindexed scalars only because a transferred basis
is still finite), so they are supplied explicitly by `let` in the
statements from those bases.  Both classes are propositions, so clients
whose context provides different instance terms can still apply the
lemmas up to defeq.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace Algebra

section QuotientMaximalIdeal

variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
  [IsLocalRing R] [Module.Finite R S] [Module.Free R S]

/-- Quotient base-change for the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication: over a local ring `R` with maximal ideal `𝔪`,
the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by the class of
`s` on `S ⧸ 𝔪S` over the residue field `R ⧸ 𝔪` is the reduction
modulo `𝔪` of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by
`s` on `S`. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_quotient_maximalIdeal_map (s : S) :
    let _ : Module.Free (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
      Module.Free.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient
        (Module.Free.chooseBasis R S))
    let _ : Module.Finite (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
      Module.Finite.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient
        (Module.Free.chooseBasis R S))
    (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul R S s).charpoly.map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) := by
  classical
  let b := Module.Free.chooseBasis R S
  have _ : Module.Free (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
    Module.Free.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
  have _ : Module.Finite (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
      (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S)) :=
    Module.Finite.of_basis (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
        (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b)
        (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
          (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s))
      = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (Algebra.lmul R S s)).map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)) := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, IsLocalRing.basisQuotient_apply]
    have hmul : (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
          (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)) (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (b j))
        = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (s * b j) := by
      simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
    rw [hmul, IsLocalRing.basisQuotient_repr]
    simp [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
  change (Algebra.lmul (R ⧸ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R)
        (S ⧸ (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R S))
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ s)).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul R S s).charpoly.map
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R))
  rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ (IsLocalRing.basisQuotient b),
    ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b, hmat, Matrix.charpoly_map]

end QuotientMaximalIdeal

section MapRingEquiv

variable {k k' E : Type*} [Field k] [Field k'] [CommRing E]
  [Algebra k' E] [Module.Finite k' E]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of left multiplication under a base-ring
equivalence: if `E` is viewed as a `k`-algebra along
`φ : k ≃+* k'`, then mapping the `k`-characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `x` along `φ` gives the `k'`-characteristic
polynomial of left multiplication by `x`. -/
theorem charpoly_lmul_map_ringEquiv (φ : k ≃+* k') (x : E) :
    letI : Algebra k E :=
      ((algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom).toAlgebra
    let _ : Module.Finite k E :=
      Module.Finite.of_basis ((Module.finBasis k' E).mapCoeffs φ.symm
        (fun c y => by
          have hmap : algebraMap k E
              = (algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom := rfl
          simp only [hmap, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.comp_apply]
          change algebraMap k' E (φ (φ.symm c)) * y
            = algebraMap k' E c * y
          rw [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]))
    (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly.map φ.toRingHom
      = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly := by
  classical
  let _ : Algebra k E :=
    ((algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom).toAlgebra
  have hsmul : ∀ (c : k) (y : E), c • y = φ c • y := fun c y => by
    have hmap : algebraMap k E
        = (algebraMap k' E).comp φ.toRingHom := rfl
    simp only [hmap, Algebra.smul_def, RingHom.comp_apply]
    rfl
  let b := Module.finBasis k' E
  let b' := b.mapCoeffs φ.symm (fun c y => by
    simpa only [RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply] using hsmul (φ.symm c) y)
  have _ : Module.Finite k E :=
    Module.Finite.of_basis b'
  have hmat : LinearMap.toMatrix b'
        b' (Algebra.lmul k E x)
      = (LinearMap.toMatrix b b (Algebra.lmul k' E x)).map
          φ.symm.toRingHom := by
    ext i j
    rw [LinearMap.toMatrix_apply, Matrix.map_apply,
      LinearMap.toMatrix_apply]
    simp only [b', Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_apply, Module.Basis.mapCoeffs_repr,
      Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul]
    rfl
  have key : (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly
      = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly.map φ.symm.toRingHom := by
    rw [← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b',
      ← LinearMap.charpoly_toMatrix _ b, hmat, Matrix.charpoly_map]
  have hcomp : φ.toRingHom.comp φ.symm.toRingHom = RingHom.id k' := by
    ext a
    simp
  change (Algebra.lmul k E x).charpoly.map φ.toRingHom
    = (Algebra.lmul k' E x).charpoly
  rw [key, Polynomial.map_map, hcomp, Polynomial.map_id]

end MapRingEquiv

end Algebra

-- Author: @toskua, Avocado
module

public import MathlibExt.LinearAlgebra.Charpoly.DependentPi

/-!
# Characteristic polynomials of left multiplication in a tower

For a tower of finite extensions of fields `k ⊆ F ⊆ E` and an element
`θ₀ : F` of the intermediate field, left multiplication on `E` by the
image of `θ₀` has characteristic polynomial over `k` equal to the
`Module.finrank F E`-th power of the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by `θ₀` on `F`:

```text
(Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly
  = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E.
```

This is leaf `B8` of the weighted branch multiplicity proof tree: for a
normalization branch, `F` is the residue field of the reduced place,
`θ₀` is the class of `X` (a primitive element of `F` over `k`, whose
characteristic polynomial on `F` over `k` is its minimal polynomial over
`k`), and `E` is the full
branch residue field, so the characteristic polynomial of the reduced
root is a power of its minimal polynomial with exponent the relative
residue degree.

## Informal proof

Choose an `F`-basis of `E` indexed by `Fin (Module.finrank F E)`
(`Module.finBasis`).  The coordinate equivalence `Module.Basis.equivFun`
identifies `E` with `Fin (finrank F E) → F` as `F`-modules, hence also
as `k`-modules after restricting scalars.  Multiplication by
`algebraMap F E θ₀` is the scalar action of `θ₀` on `E` as an
`F`-module, so in coordinates it acts componentwise as multiplication
by `θ₀` on `F` — the matrix is block-diagonal with `finrank F E`
identical blocks.  Conjugation invariance of the characteristic
polynomial and the dependent-product formula
`LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent` then give a product of
`finrank F E` copies of `(Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly`.

Only the bottom two entries of the tower need to be fields: `E` may be
any ring with compatible algebra structures.  The finiteness of `E`
over `k` is listed separately because the statement's characteristic
polynomial needs it; it follows from the other two finiteness
assumptions.
-/

@[expose] public section

set_option autoImplicit false

open Polynomial

namespace Algebra

section Tower

variable {k F E : Type*} [Field k] [Field F] [Ring E]
  [Algebra k F] [Algebra F E] [Algebra k E] [IsScalarTower k F E]
  [FiniteDimensional k F] [FiniteDimensional F E] [FiniteDimensional k E]

/-- Characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by an
intermediate-field element in a finite tower: if `θ₀` lies in the
intermediate field `F`, the characteristic polynomial of left
multiplication by its image in `E` is the `Module.finrank F E`-th power
of the characteristic polynomial of left multiplication by `θ₀` on
`F`. -/
theorem lmul_charpoly_algebraMap_tower (θ₀ : F) :
    (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly =
      (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E := by
  classical
  let n := Module.finrank F E
  let b : Module.Basis (Fin n) F E := Module.finBasis F E
  let e : E ≃ₗ[k] (Fin n → F) := b.equivFun.restrictScalars k
  have he : ∀ x i, e x i = b.repr x i := fun x i =>
    congrFun (Module.Basis.equivFun_apply b x) i
  have hconj : e.conj (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)) =
      LinearMap.pi
        (fun i => (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).comp (LinearMap.proj i)) := by
    apply LinearMap.ext
    intro y
    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := e.surjective y
    funext i
    simp only [LinearEquiv.conj_apply_apply,
      LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, LinearMap.pi_apply,
      LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, he]
    have hmul : (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)) x = θ₀ • x := by
      simp only [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul, LinearMap.mul_apply',
        Algebra.smul_def]
    rw [hmul, map_smul, Finsupp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
    simp only [Algebra.coe_lmul_eq_mul, LinearMap.mul_apply']
  calc
    (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀)).charpoly =
        (e.conj (Algebra.lmul k E (algebraMap F E θ₀))).charpoly :=
      (LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj e _).symm
    _ = ∏ _i : Fin n, (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly := by
      rw [hconj, LinearMap.charpoly_pi_dependent]
    _ = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ n := by simp
    _ = (Algebra.lmul k F θ₀).charpoly ^ Module.finrank F E := rfl

end Tower

end Algebra
